title: phlox pilosa subsp. latisepala
intro: Phlox pilosa subsp. latisepala, commonly known as wild sweet William, is a flowering plant species belonging to the phlox genus. This plant has been used in traditional medicine due to its potential health benefits, which include treating respiratory issues, such as coughs and bronchitis, as well as exhibiting anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Phlox pilosa subsp. latisepala are primarily attributed to its ability to calm the nervous system, reduce fever, and act as a diuretic. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
